newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp on track for year forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp on track for year forecasts.

text.p: Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it was on track to meet its profits forecasts for the year to June 30, 1997.
"We are on track to meet our profit forecasts, which are in line with market forecasts," Southcorp chief executive officer Graham Kraehe told reporters at a briefing.
Kraehe said market expectations were around A$130 million net profit before abnormals for the 1996/97 year.
Southcorp reported a net profit after abnormals of A$124.22 million in the 1995/96 year, which included a record second half profit of A$64.3 million.
"Each business, we expect, in the full year, as they have in the last two periods, to grow earnings over the corresponding period," Kraehe said.
Kraehe said the forecasts were dependent on there being no significant downturn in the Australian economy.
"On that basis, we are very confident that 1996/97 will be another record year for Southcorp," he said.

Recent economic data showed that the Australian economy appeared to be in an upturn. "Obviously a lift in the economy is positive for us," Kraehe said. He added the housing market is the most important market to the company particularly for its appliance and packaging businesses.
He said he did not expect interest rates to rise this year. "Our view is that we wouldn't expect a rise in interest rates this calendar year," he said.
Southcorp earlier announced a 23.4 percent rise in net profit to A$65.54 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996. -- Kevin Morrison, Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1813s
